question:
I want to study the robotics techniques described in the PDF “RT-2, Vision-Language-Action Models Transfer Web Knowledge to Robotic Control” located in my pdf/embodied_ai_papers folder.  
    Can you extract the main technical ideas from that PDF, look up the current best‑practice APIs or libraries that support similar vision‑language robotics workflows, and then save a concise summary of those findings into my long‑term memory as a new knowledge item?
answer:
Done. Here's what I found and saved.

## 1. Main technical ideas in RT-2 (arXiv:2307.15818v1, Google DeepMind, 2023)

The central claim: **a large pretrained VLM can become an end-to-end robot policy with no new architecture** — it's "co-fine-tuned" on robot trajectories plus its original web vision-language data.

**The action-as-text trick.** Actions are 6-DoF end-effector deltas (position + rotation) plus gripper extension plus a terminate flag. Each continuous dimension is discretized into 256 uniform bins, so one action = 8 integers, serialized as a string: `"1 128 91 241 5 101 127"`. Robot control is literally posed as VQA: `Q: what action should the robot take to [instruction]? A: <8 tokens>`.

**Token binding.** PaLI-X has a unique token per integer up to 1000, so bins map straight onto existing tokens. PaLM-E lacks this, so the 256 least-frequently-used tokens are overwritten — a form of symbol tuning.

**Four supporting details that actually carry the performance:**
- *Co-fine-tuning* with the original web mixture (robot data up-weighted per batch) beats robot-only fine-tuning at every model size — it prevents forgetting the visual/semantic concepts.
- *Decode-time vocabulary masking* — only valid action tokens are sampled on control prompts, full language vocab otherwise.
- *Chain-of-thought* — a `Plan:` sentence injected before the `Action:` tokens unlocks multi-stage semantic reasoning (rock as hammer, energy drink when tired).
- *Out-of-process serving* — the 55B model ran from a multi-TPU cloud service at 1–3 Hz (5B model ~5 Hz).

**Results:** ~6,000 real trials. Seen tasks ≈ RT-1, but **~2x better generalization** to unseen objects/backgrounds/environments than RT-1 and MOO, ~6x over weaker baselines, and >3x on emergent symbol/reasoning/person tasks. Ablations: from-scratch training fails even at 5B; bigger models generalize better.

**Honest limitation:** it learns no new *physical skills* — only new ways to deploy the ones in the robot data.

## 2. Current best-practice tooling

- **LeRobot v0.6.1** (`/huggingface/lerobot`) is the closest thing to a maintained implementation of this whole pipeline: `lerobot-train --policy.type=smolvla --policy.load_vlm_weights=true` (the direct analogue of RT-2's VLM-initialized backbone), pi0/pi0.5 as the larger VLAs, and `lerobot-rollout` for deployment. Notably, RT-2's headline limitation is now solved at the *inference* layer rather than the model layer — **Real-Time Chunking** (`--inference.type=rtc`, `execution_horizon`, `max_guidance_weight`) makes a 1–3 Hz VLA execute smoothly.
- **Transformers** (`AutoModelForImageTextToText` + `AutoProcessor` with Qwen2.5-VL / SmolVLM, `apply_chat_template` with the image inline) is the practical way to build and fine-tune the backbone stage.

## 3. Saved to long-term memory

Created 4 entities and 6 relations (the graph was empty before):

- **RT-2: Vision-Language-Action Models (Brohan et al., 2023)** — 16 observations, the full technical breakdown
- **LeRobot (Hugging Face)** and **Hugging Face Transformers (multimodal backbone)** — 8 and 7 observations of verified API details
- **"VLA Robotics Playbook: RT-2 ideas mapped to current tooling (2026-11-01)"** — the concise summary item you asked for, linked to the other three

Two caveats I recorded rather than papered over: OpenVLA and the openpi (pi0) ecosystem are the other obvious reference implementations but I could not documentation-verify them in this pass, and LeRobot's SmolVLA/pi0 action encoders may assume normalized joint or EEF deltas — worth checking before porting RT-2's 8-token string format wholesale. (The `list-popular-libraries` tool errored out with a config issue, so library discovery went via explicit resolution instead.)

content.text:
### Train policy with RA-BC weighting using lerobot-train

Source: https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/blob/main/docs/source/sarm.mdx

Trains a policy (e.g., PI0) with RA-BC sample weighting. The progress file is auto-detected from the dataset path (sarm_progress.parquet) if not explicitly provided. Supported policies: PI0, PI0.5, SmolVLA.

```bash
lerobot-train \
  --dataset.repo_id=your-username/your-dataset \
  --policy.type=pi0 \
  --sample_weighting.type=rabc \
  --sample_weighting.head_mode=sparse \
  --sample_weighting.kappa=0.01 \
  --output_dir=outputs/train/policy_rabc \
  --batch_size=32 \
  --steps=40000
```

--------------------------------

### Train SmolVLA on LIBERO with lerobot-train

Source: https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/blob/main/docs/source/libero.mdx

Train SmolVLA on the recommended lerobot/libero dataset. Requires a video backend (torchcodec or pyav) and pins the dataset revision for reproducible results. Replace --policy.push_to_hub=false with --policy.repo_id=${HF_USER}/libero-smolvla to share the result on the Hub.

```bash
lerobot-train \
  --policy.type=smolvla \
  --policy.load_vlm_weights=true \
  --policy.push_to_hub=false \
  --dataset.repo_id=lerobot/libero \
  --dataset.video_backend=torchcodec \
  --output_dir=./outputs/libero_smolvla \
  --steps=100000 \
  --batch_size=64
```

--------------------------------

### Run rollout with Real-Time Chunking (--inference.type=rtc)

Source: https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/blob/main/docs/source/inference.mdx

Run a rollout with the Real-Time Chunking (RTC) inference backend. Use this for large, slow VLA models like Pi0, Pi0.5, or SmolVLA to achieve smooth, continuous motion despite high inference latency. The example sets an execution horizon of 10 and a max guidance weight of 10.0; other RTC flags (mode, prefix_attention_schedule, queue_threshold) are available and documented in the table.

```bash
lerobot-rollout \
    --strategy.type=base \
    --inference.type=rtc \
    --inference.rtc.execution_horizon=10 \
    --inference.rtc.max_guidance_weight=10.0 \
    --policy.path=${HF_USER}/pi0_policy \
    --robot.type=so100_follower \
    --robot.port=/dev/ttyACM0 \
    --robot.cameras="{ front: {type: opencv, index_or_path: 0, width: 640, height: 480, fps: 30}}" \
    --task="Pick up the cube" \
    --duration=60 \
    --device=cuda
```

--------------------------------

### Train SmolVLA on LIBERO-plus

Source: https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/blob/main/docs/source/libero_plus.mdx

Train a SmolVLA policy on the LIBERO-plus dataset. Requires the lerobot/libero_plus dataset and sets --env.type=libero_plus with the task libero_spatial. Uses 100000 steps, batch size 4, and evaluates every 1000 steps.

```bash
lerobot-train \
    --policy.type=smolvla \
    --policy.repo_id=${HF_USER}/smolvla_libero_plus \
    --policy.load_vlm_weights=true \
    --dataset.repo_id=lerobot/libero_plus \
    --env.type=libero_plus \
    --env.task=libero_spatial \
    --output_dir=./outputs/ \
    --steps=100000 \
    --batch_size=4 \
    --eval.batch_size=1 \
    --eval.n_episodes=1 \
    --env_eval_freq=1000
```

--------------------------------

### Run inference with lerobot-rollout (base and sentry modes)

Source: https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/blob/main/docs/source/il_robots.mdx

Two rollout strategies for deploying a trained policy with lerobot-rollout. Base mode runs autonomous rollout without recording; Sentry mode records episodes and auto-uploads every 5 episodes to the specified dataset repo. Both load the model from --policy.path and use the same SO-100 follower robot and camera setup.

```bash
lerobot-rollout \
  --strategy.type=base \
  --policy.path=${HF_USER}/my_policy \
  --robot.type=so100_follower \
  --robot.port=/dev/ttyACM1 \
  --robot.cameras="{ up: {type: opencv, index_or_path: /dev/video10, width: 640, height: 480, fps: 30}, side: {type: intelrealsense, serial_number_or_name: 233522074606, width: 640, height: 480, fps: 30}}" \
  --task="Put lego brick into the transparent box" \
  --duration=60
```

```bash
lerobot-rollout \
  --strategy.type=sentry \
  --strategy.upload_every_n_episodes=5 \
  --policy.path=${HF_USER}/my_policy \
  --robot.type=so100_follower \
  --robot.port=/dev/ttyACM1 \
  --robot.cameras="{ up: {type: opencv, index_or_path: /dev/video10, width: 640, height: 480, fps: 30}, side: {type: intelrealsense, serial_number_or_name: 233522074606, width: 640, height: 480, fps: 30}}" \
  --dataset.repo_id=${HF_USER}/eval_so100 \
  --dataset.single_task="Put lego brick into the transparent box" \
  --duration=600
```

### Prepare Image Chat Messages with apply_chat_template (Python)

Source: https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/v4.56.2/en/chat_templating_multimodal

Demonstrates preparing chat messages containing text and image data for multimodal models using apply_chat_template. It initializes a model and processor, defines a chat message structure, tokenizes the input, and shows the keys present in the processed output, including 'pixel_values' for image data. This is essential for feeding multimodal inputs to the model.

```python
from transformers import AutoProcessor, AutoModelForImageTextToText

model = AutoModelForImageTextToText.from_pretrained("Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct", device_map="auto", torch_dtype="auto")
processor = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained("Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct")

messages = [
    {
      "role": "system",
      "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "You are a friendly chatbot who always responds in the style of a pirate"}],
    },
    {
      "role": "user",
      "content": [
            {"type": "image", "url": "http://images.cocodataset.org/val2017/000000039769.jpg"},
            {"type": "text", "text": "What are these?"},
        ],
    },
]

processed_chat = processor.apply_chat_template(messages, add_generation_prompt=True, tokenize=True, return_dict=True, return_tensors="pt")
print(list(processed_chat.keys()))

out = model.generate(**processed_chat.to(model.device), max_new_tokens=128)
print(processor.decode(out[0]))
```

--------------------------------

### Qwen2.5-VL Chat Template without Vision IDs

Source: https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/v4.56.2/en/model_doc/qwen2_5_vl

Demonstrates applying a chat template for the Qwen2.5-VL model without adding specific vision IDs. This is useful for structuring conversations involving text and image/video placeholders. The output is a formatted string ready for model input.

```python
import torch
from transformers import Qwen2_5_VLForConditionalGeneration, AutoProcessor

model = Qwen2_5_VLForConditionalGeneration.from_pretrained(
    "Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct",
    dtype=torch.float16,
    device_map="auto",
    attn_implementation="sdpa"
)
processor = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained("Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct")
conversation = [
    {
        "role": "user",
        "content": [
            {"type": "image"},
            {"type": "text", "text": "Hello, how are you?"}
        ]
    },
    {
        "role": "assistant",
        "content": "I'm doing well, thank you for asking. How can I assist you today?"
    },
    {
        "role": "user",
        "content": [
            {"type": "text", "text": "Can you describe these images and video?"},
            {"type": "image"},
            {"type": "image"},
            {"type": "video"},
            {"type": "text", "text": "These are from my vacation."}
        ]
    },
    {
        "role": "assistant",
        "content": "I'd be happy to describe the images and video for you. Could you please provide more context about your vacation?"
    },
    {
        "role": "user",
        "content": "It was a trip to the mountains. Can you see the details in the images and video?"
    }
]

# default:
prompt_without_id = processor.apply_chat_template(conversation, add_generation_prompt=True)
# Excepted output: '<|im_start|>system\nYou are a helpful assistant.<|im_end|>\n<|im_start|>user\n<|vision_start|><|image_pad|><|vision_end|>Hello, how are you?<|im_end|>\n<|im_start|>assistant\nI'm doing well, thank you for asking. How can I assist you today?<|im_end|>\n<|im_start|>user\nCan you describe these images and video?<|vision_start|><|image_pad|><|vision_end|><|vision_start|><|image_pad|><|vision_end|><|vision_start|><|video_pad|><|vision_end|>These are from my vacation.<|im_end|>\n<|im_start|>assistant\nI'd be happy to describe the images and video for you. Could you please provide more context about your vacation?<|im_end|>\n<|im_start|>user\nIt was a trip to the mountains. Can you see the details in the images and video?<|im_end|>\n<|im_start|>assistant\n'
```

--------------------------------

### Inference > Generation of the output

Source: https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/v4.56.2/en/model_doc/qwen2_5_vl

The `apply_chat_template` method in the processor can be used to format conversations for the Qwen2.5-VL model. You can choose to either include or exclude vision IDs in the formatted prompt. The `add_generation_prompt` parameter ensures that the prompt is prepared for text generation, while `add_vision_id` can be set to `True` to prepend labels like 'Picture 1:' or 'Video 1:' to the corresponding vision tokens.

--------------------------------

### Qwen2.5-VL Chat Template with Vision IDs

Source: https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/v4.56.2/en/model_doc/qwen2_5_vl

Shows how to apply a chat template for the Qwen2.5-VL model, including 'add_vision_id=True' to assign labels like 'Picture 1' and 'Video 1' to multimodal content. This enhances clarity when processing multiple images or videos in a conversation.

```python
# add ids
prompt_with_id = processor.apply_chat_template(conversation, add_generation_prompt=True, add_vision_id=True)
# Excepted output: '<|im_start|>system\nYou are a helpful assistant.<|im_end|>\n<|im_start|>user\nPicture 1: <|vision_start|><|image_pad|><|vision_end|>Hello, how are you?<|im_end|>\n<|im_start|>assistant\nI'm doing well, thank you for asking. How can I assist you today?<|im_end|>\n<|im_start|>user\nCan you describe these images and video?Picture 2: <|vision_start|><|image_pad|><|vision_end|>Picture 3: <|vision_start|><|image_pad|><|vision_end|>Video 1: <|vision_start|><|video_pad|><|vision_end|>These are from my vacation.<|im_end|>\n<|im_start|>assistant\nI'd be happy to describe the images and video for you. Could you please provide more context about your vacation?<|im_end|>\n<|im_start|>user\nIt was a trip to the mountains. Can you see the details in the images and video?<|im_end|>\n<|im_start|>assistant\n'
```

--------------------------------

### Processors > Multi-modal processors > class transformers.ProcessorMixin > apply_chat_template

Source: https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/v4.56.2/en/main_classes/processors

Similar to the `apply_chat_template` method on tokenizers, this method applies a Jinja template to input conversations to turn them into a single tokenizable string. The input is expected to be in the following format, where each message content is a list consisting of text and optionally image or video inputs. One can also provide an image, video, URL or local path which will be used to form `pixel_values` when `return_dict=True`. If not provided, one will get only the formatted text, optionally tokenized text.

entities.name: RT-2: Vision-Language-Action Models (Brohan et al., 2023)
observations: Source: Google DeepMind technical report, arXiv:2307.15818v1 (28 Jul 2023), 26 pages; project site robotics-transformer2.github.io.

Core thesis: a large pretrained vision-language model (VLM) can be co-fine-tuned directly into an end-to-end robotic policy with no new architecture or action-specific layers, producing a Vision-Language-Action (VLA) model.
Recipe: co-fine-tune on (a) robot trajectory data and (b) the original Internet-scale VLM data (VQA, captioning, interleaved image-text), rather than fine-tuning on robot data alone.

Key trick - actions as text: the action space is 6-DoF end-effector delta position + delta rotation, gripper extension, and a terminate flag. Every continuous dimension is discretized into 256 uniform bins, giving 8 integers serialized as the string 'terminate dx dy dz drx dry drz gripper' (e.g. '1 128 91 241 5 101 127').

Token binding: PaLI-X has a unique token for each integer up to 1000, so action bins map onto the existing integer tokens; PaLM-E lacks this, so the 256 least-frequently-used tokens are overwritten to form the action vocabulary (a form of symbol tuning).
Input/target format: image + 'Q: what action should the robot take to [task instruction]? A: <action tokens>' - i.e. robot control is cast as visual question answering.

Output constraint: at decode time the vocabulary is restricted to valid action tokens whenever the model is prompted with a robot-action task, while the full natural-language vocabulary is retained for standard VLM tasks. This guarantees executable actions.
Data balancing: robot and web data are mixed in each batch with an increased sampling weight on the robot dataset to keep both abstract visual concepts and low-level actions in view.

Instantiations: RT-2-PaLI-X at 5B and 55B parameters, RT-2-PaLM-E at 12B; the 55B model is claimed to be the largest model ever used for direct closed-loop robot control (by over an order of magnitude at the time).

Real-time inference: models are served from a multi-TPU cloud service queried over the network, achieving ~1-3 Hz for the 55B model and ~5 Hz for the 5B model, with one service supporting multiple robots.

Empirical results: ~6,000 real-world evaluation trials on a 7-DoF mobile manipulator. Seen-task performance is comparable to RT-1 (35M params), but generalization to unseen objects/backgrounds/environments is ~2x better than RT-1 and MOO and ~6x better than other baselines.

Emergent capabilities transferred from web pretraining: symbol understanding (e.g. 'move apple to 3', 'push coke can on top of heart'), reasoning (same-color matching, arithmetic goals, multilingual instructions), and human recognition (e.g. 'move the coke can to the person with glasses') - over 3x the average success of the best baseline.

Ablations: training a large VLM from scratch performs poorly even at 5B; co-fine-tuning generalizes better than robot-only fine-tuning at every size; larger models generalize better. PaLM-E variant wins on math reasoning, PaLI-X on symbol/person tasks, attributed to different pretraining mixtures.

Chain-of-thought variant: a PaLM-E RT-2 model fine-tuned for a few hundred steps on data augmented with a 'Plan:' sentence before the 'Action:' tokens (e.g. 'Instruction: I'm hungry. Plan: pick rxbar chocolate. Action: ...') elicits multi-stage semantic reasoning, e.g. choosing a rock as an improvised hammer or an energy drink for a tired person.
Simulation check: a PaLI-3B RT-2 variant on the open-source Language-Table benchmark scores 90 +/- 10 vs 77 +/- 4 for LAVA and 74 +/- 13 for RT-1.

Limitations stated by the authors: no new physical skills are acquired (the motion repertoire is bounded by the robot data - only the deployment of those skills generalizes); inference compute is expensive and may bottleneck high-frequency control; very few VLMs are available with fine-tuning APIs, which limits who can build VLAs.

entities.name: LeRobot (Hugging Face)
observations: Context7 library ID /huggingface/lerobot, current version v0.6.1, High source reputation, ~4.5k code snippets. Positioned as end-to-end learning for robotics.
Ships production VLA and imitation-learning policies behind one CLI: policy.type values include pi0, pi0.5, smolvla, plus ACT/Diffusion-style baselines.

Training is a single command, e.g. 'lerobot-train --policy.type=smolvla --policy.load_vlm_weights=true --dataset.repo_id=lerobot/libero --dataset.video_backend=torchcodec --output_dir=./outputs/libero_smolvla --steps=100000 --batch_size=64'. load_vlm_weights=true is the direct analogue of RT-2's VLM-initialized backbone.

Deployment is also a single command: 'lerobot-rollout --policy.path=${HF_USER}/my_policy --robot.type=so100_follower --robot.port=/dev/ttyACM0 --robot.cameras="{front: {type: opencv, index_or_path: 0, width: 640, height: 480, fps: 30}}" --task="Pick up the cube" --duration=60'.

Real-Time Chunking addresses exactly RT-2's 1-3 Hz latency problem: '--inference.type=rtc --inference.rtc.execution_horizon=10 --inference.rtc.max_guidance_weight=10.0' lets slow, large VLAs produce smooth continuous motion; modes, prefix_attention_schedule and queue_threshold are tunable.

Quality-weighted imitation: --sample_weighting.type=rabc (Recursive/RA-BC style) with --sample_weighting.kappa and head_mode=sparse reweights demonstrations; supported for pi0, pi0.5, SmolVLA. Useful where teleop data quality varies.

Rollout strategies: 'base' (autonomous, no recording) and 'sentry' (records episodes, auto-uploads every N episodes via --strategy.upload_every_n_episodes to a dataset repo) - a built-in human-in-the-loop data flywheel.
Datasets/policies live on the HF Hub, so dataset versioning (including pinning a dataset revision for reproducibility) and policy sharing are first-class.

entities.name: Hugging Face Transformers (multimodal backbone)
observations: Context7 library ID /huggingface/transformers (also indexed at /websites/huggingface_co_transformers_v4_56_2_en), High reputation, 8k+ snippets.

The practical way to obtain and fine-tune the VLM backbone that an RT-2-style VLA needs: AutoModelForImageTextToText + AutoProcessor, e.g. Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct or Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct, or SmolVLM for small on-robot budgets.

Canonical multimodal call: messages = [{role, content:[{type:'image', url/path}, {type:'text', text}]}]; processed = processor.apply_chat_template(messages, add_generation_prompt=True, tokenize=True, return_dict=True, return_tensors='pt'); out = model.generate(**processed.to(model.device), max_new_tokens=128); processor.decode(out[0]). Passing the image inside apply_chat_template is what produces pixel_values.
apply_chat_template accepts an image URL or local path directly and returns pixel_values when return_dict=True; otherwise it returns only formatted (optionally tokenized) text.
For multi-image prompts use add_vision_id=True to prefix 'Picture 1:', 'Picture 2:' - relevant for multi-camera robot setups.
Loader flags seen in current docs: dtype=torch.float16, device_map='auto', attn_implementation='sdpa' (the 'dtype' argument replaces the older torch_dtype in recent versions).

Because actions can be emitted as plain tokens, the RT-2 co-fine-tuning recipe is expressible as an ordinary supervised fine-tuning job over 'Q: what action should the robot take to <instruction>? A: <8 integer tokens>' chat samples.

entities.name: VLA Robotics Playbook: RT-2 ideas mapped to current tooling (2026-11-01)
observations: SUMMARY - RT-2 (Google DeepMind, arXiv:2307.15818v1, 2023) shows that a large pretrained VLM can be turned into an end-to-end robot policy by co-fine-tuning it on robot trajectories AND its original web vision-language data, encoding each action as 8 text tokens (256 uniform bins over 6-DoF delta pose + gripper + terminate). No new architecture is needed; the win is generalization and semantic reasoning inherited from the web pretraining, not new motor skills.

The five ideas worth reusing: (1) action-as-text tokenization so the same weights, loss and vocabulary cover language and control; (2) co-fine-tuning with the original web mixture, with robot data up-weighted in each batch, which prevents catastrophic forgetting and is measurably better than robot-only fine-tuning; (3) decode-time vocabulary masking to only valid action tokens for control prompts; (4) a chain-of-thought 'Plan:' prefix before the action tokens to unlock multi-stage semantic reasoning; (5) serving the big model out-of-process (cloud/multi-TPU) rather than on-robot - RT-2 got 1-3 Hz at 55B and ~5 Hz at 5B.

Reported numbers to calibrate expectations: seen tasks ~= RT-1, but ~2x better generalization than RT-1/MOO and ~6x better than weaker baselines over ~6k trials; >3x on emergent symbol/reasoning/person tasks; 90 +/- 10 vs 77 +/- 4 on Language-Table simulation. Bigger models generalize better at every size tested.

HOW TO BUILD IT TODAY - start with LeRobot (v0.6.1) rather than reimplementing: 'lerobot-train --policy.type=smolvla --policy.load_vlm_weights=true --dataset.repo_id=<you>/<dataset> --steps=100000' trains a VLM-initialized VLA, and 'lerobot-rollout --policy.path=<you>/<policy> --robot.type=so100_follower --robot.cameras=... --task="..."' deploys it. pi0 / pi0.5 are the larger VLA options; ACT/Diffusion are the cheap baselines to beat.

Latency, RT-2's main practical limitation, is now solved at the inference layer instead of the model layer: LeRobot Real-Time Chunking (--inference.type=rtc with execution_horizon and max_guidance_weight) makes slow large VLAs execute smoothly, so the 1-3 Hz regime is usable.

Backbone stage: use Transformers AutoModelForImageTextToText + AutoProcessor (Qwen2.5-VL-3B/7B-Instruct, or SmolVLM for small footprints) and apply_chat_template with the image inline to build exactly the 'Q: what action should the robot take to <instruction>? A: <tokens>' samples RT-2 trains on; add_vision_id=True when several cameras are in the prompt.

Data strategy: collect demonstrations with a real robot into a LeRobotDataset on the HF Hub (pin the dataset revision for reproducibility), keep a web/VQA mixture alongside so co-fine-tuning stays possible, and use --sample_weighting.type=rabc to down-weight low-quality teleop. A 'sentry' rollout records and uploads episodes every N, giving a continuous data flywheel.

Design cautions carried over from RT-2's limitations: web pretraining does not add new motor skills, only new ways to deploy existing ones, so skill coverage comes from data collection breadth (the paper points at human video as the next frontier); keep the action discretization/token mapping stable so checkpoints and datasets remain compatible; validate the decode-time action-token mask explicitly, since an unconstrained VLM can emit non-executable text; and budget for inference cost/quantization before promising high control rates.

Open items / to verify before committing: OpenVLA and the openpi (pi0) ecosystem are the other obvious reference implementations but were not documentation-verified in this pass; check whether LeRobot's SmolVLA/pi0 action encoders assume normalized joint or EEF deltas before porting RT-2's 8-token string format wholesale.
